title: Webb's advice on playing around the melody
summary: Webb tells him not to compete with Black jazz trumpeters but to play around the melody like Red Nichols, giving the section three styles.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You were playing solo trumpet as well, were you?

All right. Yeah, you know, solo, my own style. He didn't want me to mess around with the jazz like the other trumpet player, because one day he said -- I told him -- he said, never mind that stuff you want to play with Louie. Never mind that. You've got to develop yourself into something else because, see, every Negro trumpet player can outplay you that kind of stuff, because that's their usual. They match you in that.

What I want you to do, do you hear those white trumpet players when they play jazz, like Red Nichols and (inaudible) they play around the melody. That's what I want you to do, what none of those guys do; they play something else. So that's what I want you to do, develop the very, start simple, you fool around with the melody, just little bit, jazz around the melody. Don't try to do that hard stuff because you won't outdo them.

They had a guy named Bobby Scott playing second (inaudible). He said, you aren't going to outdo those guys. So try to get a start like that. I've got three different styles in my trumpet section, and I'll be able to work my music different ways. All right, great.
